title: Designing an honest benchmark
summary: Baselines, ablations, leakage-free splits, simulability checks, the full resource bill, statistics, and the reporting guidelines oncology journals expect — TRIPOD+AI, REMARK, CONSORT-AI and SPIRIT-AI.

shots.title:
An honest
benchmark.
shots.subtitle: Decide the rules before you see the results.
shots.narration: Your benchmark is your paper's spine. Design it before you run anything, and write down the rules — referees from both fields will check them.

shots.heading: Seven components — the comparison
items: **Splits** — every fitted step inside training data
shots.narration: Seven components. First, the comparison: strong, equally tuned classical baselines; ablations that remove the quantum ingredient; splits that keep every fitted step inside the training data; and a statement of what a classical simulator could do.

shots.heading: Seven components — the accounting
items: **Reporting** — the right guideline; code and data
shots.narration: Then the accounting: the full resource bill, proper statistics with several seeds and confidence intervals, and reporting to the right guideline with code and data shared.

shots.text: Remove **entanglement**; add a **random control**. If nothing changes, quantumness isn't doing the work.
shots.narration: Ablations are the most persuasive experiment you can run. Remove the entanglement — a large benchmark found it often made no difference. Add a random control — in one TCGA study, random bit-strings matched the quantum device.

shots.text: Every fitted step — normalisation, feature selection, feature maps, hyperparameters — goes **inside** the training folds.
shots.narration: Splits: every fitted step — normalisation, feature selection, feature-map parameters, hyperparameters — happens inside the training folds. You saw in the lab what happens otherwise.

shots.text: Simulability: **16 qubits** is a megabyte. State what a classical simulator can do at your scale.
shots.narration: Simulability: state plainly what a classical simulator could do at your scale. Sixteen qubits is about a megabyte; thirty is seventeen gigabytes. If your circuit fits, say so, and run the simulation as a control.

shots.text: Resources: report the **whole bill** — about **10⁸ measurements** for a 4-qubit VQE in our lab.
shots.narration: Resources: report the whole bill — shots, repetitions, queue and wall-clock time, and the classical pre- and post-processing. In this course's lab, a four-qubit VQE to chemical accuracy took about a hundred million measurements.

shots.text: Baselines get the **same budget**. In radiotherapy, simulated annealing beat the quantum annealer on plan quality.
shots.narration: Baselines get the same tuning and time budget, and include the best classical heuristic. In the radiotherapy study, simulated annealing produced better plans than the quantum annealer — the kind of result a fair comparison reveals.

shots.heading: Guidelines oncology journals expect
shots.narration: Then report to the guideline your field expects: TRIPOD plus AI, twenty-seven items, for prediction models; REMARK for tumour-marker studies; CONSORT-AI and SPIRIT-AI, adding fourteen and fifteen items, for trials and protocols of AI interventions.

shots.text: Why so strict? Replicated cancer-biology effects were a median **85%** smaller than the originals.
shots.narration: Why such strictness? Because the base rate is sobering: when cancer-biology experiments were repeated, effects were a median eighty-five percent smaller than first reported. Pre-specified benchmarks are how you avoid becoming that statistic.

shots.text: Share code and data **FAIR**ly — findable, accessible, interoperable, reusable.
shots.narration: And share your code and data following FAIR principles, within the limits of patient-data access rules, so that someone else can rerun your benchmark.

steps.title: Order the protocol
steps.brief: Put the steps of a pre-specified benchmark in order.

items.label: Fix the question, the primary metric and the falsifying result
Lock away an external test set before any analysis
Choose classical baselines and give every method the same tuning budget
Split the training data into folds; keep every fitted step inside them
Run quantum and classical methods plus ablations over several seeds
Evaluate once on the locked external set
Report confidence intervals, the resource bill and the guideline checklist

steps.title: Benchmark protocol
steps.brief: The methods heart of your proposal. Write it as if you will be held to it.

fields.label: Primary metric and how it maps to a clinical or chemical quantity.
Data and splits: sources, sizes, access route, external test set, where each fitted step happens.
Classical baselines and the shared tuning/time budget.
Ablations and controls (e.g. no entanglement, random control, classical simulation of the circuit).
Resource accounting: qubits, depth, shots, runtime, classical processing.
Statistics: seeds, confidence intervals, sample-size or power reasoning.
Reporting guideline you will follow
options: None fits — explained in the protocol

questions.prompt: You develop a prediction model for treatment response using machine learning. Which guideline applies?
questions.explain: TRIPOD+AI covers clinical prediction models built with regression or machine learning (27 items).

questions.prompt: How many items does the TRIPOD+AI checklist have?
Removing entanglement from your quantum model doesn't change accuracy. You should…
options: Leave the ablation out of the paper
Report it: it says the quantum ingredient isn't driving performance
Add more qubits until it matters
questions.explain: Ablations are evidence either way; hiding them is a reproducibility failure.
